bib.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos

read.skipped: Read all prose, tables, appendices A-H; per-dataset plot axis numbers (Figs 12-15) and Table 17 cell values and reference list were only skimmed (numeric chart residue).

question: Can the Segment Anything promptable segmentation model be extended to a unified model for images and videos, with a memory mechanism and a large video segmentation dataset built by a model-in-the-loop data engine?
hypothesis: A SAM generalisation with streaming memory, trained on a large diverse video dataset collected with the model in the loop, gives more accurate and more interaction-efficient video segmentation, and image segmentation as good as SAM but faster.
contributions: Promptable Visual Segmentation (PVS) task generalising image segmentation to video
SAM 2 model: simple transformer with streaming memory for real-time video processing
Data engine with SAM 2 in the loop, 8.4x faster than per-frame SAM annotation
SA-V dataset: 50.9K videos, 642.6K masklets, 35.5M masks, released CC BY 4.0
Release of model checkpoints, training code (Apache 2.0) and demo code

method.summary: SAM 2 keeps SAM's prompt encoder and two-way mask decoder, replaces the ViT with an MAE-pretrained Hiera image encoder, and inserts memory attention that conditions each frame's embedding on a FIFO memory bank of spatial memories plus object pointers; images are single-frame videos. It is pre-trained on SA-1B then trained jointly on video (SA-V, Internal, optional open VOS) and image data with simulated interactive prompting.
method.task: promptable visual segmentation in images and videos (interactive and semi-supervised VOS, SA task)

datasets.name: SA-1B
datasets.size: images, 10% subset used in full training; full for pre-training
datasets.preprocessing: filter masks covering >90% of image; 64 random masks per image; hflip; resize 1024x1024

datasets.name: SA-V
datasets.size: 50.9K videos, 642.6K masklets (190.9K manual, 451.7K auto), 35.5M masks, 196.0 hr, 4.2M frames
datasets.split: train/val/test split by video author and geography; val 155 videos 293 masklets; test 150 videos 278 masklets
datasets.source: crowdworker videos, CC BY 4.0; annotated at 6 FPS
datasets.preprocessing: only manual masklets used for training

datasets.name: Internal
datasets.size: 62.9K videos, 69.6K masklets for training; Internal-test 96 videos 189 masklets
datasets.source: internally available licensed video data, Phase 2/3 annotated (test Phase 1)

datasets.name: DAVIS, MOSE, YouTubeVOS
datasets.split: mixture ~1.3% DAVIS, ~9.4% MOSE, ~9.2% YouTubeVOS in the open-source mixture

datasets.name: MOSE dev
datasets.size: 200 randomly-sampled videos from MOSE training split, excluded from training

datasets.name: 17 zero-shot video datasets (9 dense + 8 sparse)
datasets.source: EndoVis 2018, ESD, LVOSv2, LV-VIS, UVO, VOST, PUMaVOS, Virtual KITTI 2, VIPSeg, Wildfires, VISOR, FBMS, Ego-Exo4D, Cityscapes, Lindenthal Camera, HT1080WT, Drosophila Heart

datasets.name: 37 zero-shot image datasets (SA-23 + 14 video-derived)
datasets.source: SAM's 23 plus frames from 14 video datasets

models.name: SAM 2 (Hiera-B+) default
models.architecture: Hiera image encoder + FPN, memory attention (L=4 layers, self+cross attention + MLP), SAM prompt encoder, two-way mask decoder with occlusion head, memory encoder, memory bank
models.hidden: 256 channel embeddings; memory features projected to 64 dim; 256-dim object pointer split into 4 tokens of 64
models.context: N=6 recent frames (ablation default), M prompted frames; 8-frame training sequences

models.name: SAM+XMem++ and SAM+Cutie
models.architecture: SAM for click/box prompts, XMem++ or Cutie (modified to take mask inputs on multiple frames) for propagation

training.objective: linear combination of focal and dice loss for masks, MAE (L1) loss for IoU prediction, cross-entropy for occlusion/object prediction, weight ratio 20:1:1:1; only the lowest-loss mask supervised for multi-mask outputs; no supervision of masks on frames with no ground-truth mask but occlusion head always supervised
training.optimizer: AdamW, beta1,beta2=0.9,0.999, gradient clipping l2 max 0.1, layer-wise decay
training.lr: pre-training 4e-4; full training img. enc.: 6e-5, other: 3.0e-4; 16-frame fine-tune: half of original
training.lr_schedule: pre-training reciprocal sqrt timescale=1000, linear cooldown 5k iters; full training cosine
training.warmup: pre-training linear 1k iters; full training linear 7.5k iters
training.steps: ~90k pre-training on SA-1B; ~150k full training; 50k fine-tune on 16-frame sequences (1/3 of original schedule); 200k in Table 7 ablations
training.seq_len: 8 frames per training sequence (up to 2 prompted, up to 3 masklets); 16-frame fine-tuning
training.regularisation: augmentation: hflip, affine (deg 25, shear 20), colorjitter (b 0.1, c 0.03, s 0.03), grayscale 0.05, per-frame colorjitter (b 0.1, c 0.05, s 0.05), mosaic 2x2 with prob 0.1; temporal reversal prob 0.5

other.data_mix_with_open_VOS: ~1.3% DAVIS, ~9.4% MOSE, ~9.2% YouTubeVOS, ~15.5% SA-1B, ~49.5% SA-V, ~15.1% Internal
other.initial_prompt: ground-truth mask p=0.5, positive click p=0.25, box p=0.25
other.correction_clicks: 7; 10% chance sampled from ground truth irrespective of prediction
other.pretrain_changes_vs_SAM: L1 IoU loss, sigmoid on IoU logits, no no-prompt iterations, 7 correction clicks instead of 8
other.alternating_batches: each iteration samples a full batch from image or video data, probability proportional to source size
other.released_model: trained on SA-V manual + Internal and SA-1B
other.16-frame_finetune: top 50% most-edited masklets of SA-V and Internal, image encoder frozen

inference.decoding: multiple masks predicted per frame under ambiguity; mask with highest predicted IoU is propagated if no further prompt
inference.samples: each object inferred independently in multi-object videos; single deterministic run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: positive/negative clicks, boxes, or masks on any frame; interactive eval places first click at the mask centre (pixel with largest distance to boundary) and further clicks at centre of error region

parameters.annotation_time_model: Tloc=1 s, Tclick=1.5 s, Texam=30 s per 300-frame video

other.speed: single A100, PyTorch 2.3.1, CUDA 12.1, bfloat16 autocast, torch.compile on image encoder; batch 10 for image FPS, batch 1 for video
other.auto_masklets: 32x32 grid on first frame plus 16x16 on 4 zoomed crops and 4x4 on 16 zoomed crops; remove components <200 px, fill holes <200 px

metrics.name: J&F
metrics.definition: standard VOS region similarity and boundary accuracy (Pont-Tuset 2017); J only on VOST; G on YTVOS 2019

metrics.name: mIoU
metrics.definition: mean IoU for SA task at 1 and 5 clicks

metrics.name: FPS
metrics.definition: frames per second on one A100

metrics.name: Phase 1 Mask Alignment Score
metrics.definition: percentage of masks whose IoU with the Phase 1 masks exceeds 0.75

metrics.name: J&F@60s / AUC-J&F

eval.protocol: Offline: multiple passes, next prompt on worst-IoU frame. Online: single pass, pause at frame with IoU<0.75 and add clicks. 9 dense zero-shot datasets, Nclick=3. VOS: 1/3/5 clicks, box or mask on first frame over 17 datasets. No seeds or significance tests.

availability.weights: SAM 2 checkpoints released (note: results use SAM 2.1 version)

evidence.quote: All the results presented in this paper are based on a new version of SAM 2 (improved over our initial release; denoted as “SAM 2.1” in https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2)

results.claim: SAM 2 gives better interactive video segmentation accuracy with more than 3x fewer interactions than SAM+XMem++ / SAM+Cutie baselines
results.setup: Promptable video segmentation, 9 zero-shot densely annotated video datasets, 3 clicks per frame, offline and online, Nframe=1..8, Hiera-B+ at 1024
results.quote: Overall, SAM 2 can generate better segmentation accuracy, with >3× fewer interactions.

results.claim: Data engine Phase 3 (SAM 2 in loop) is 8.4x faster per frame than Phase 1 (SAM only)
results.setup: Controlled experiment, 169 videos and 452 masklets, three annotator subsets (E.2.2); 4.5 s vs 37.8 s per frame
results.quote: Phase 3 with SAM 2 in the loop leads to increased efficiency and comparable quality: it is 8.4× faster than Phase 1

results.claim: Annotation time per frame fell from 37.8 s (Phase 1) to 7.4 s (Phase 2) to 4.5 s (Phase 3)

limits: May fail to segment objects across shot changes and can lose track or confuse objects in crowded scenes, after long occlusions or in extended videos (App C).
Struggles with thin or fine details especially when fast-moving, and with nearby similar-looking objects; explicit motion modelling suggested.
Each object processed separately with only shared per-frame embeddings, no inter-object communication.
Data engine still relies on human annotators to verify masklet quality and select frames to correct.
On DAVIS interactive, SAM 2 tends to segment parts at first click while DAVIS has whole objects, which may penalise it.
1-click fairness gap (male 81.9 vs female 75.1) partly attributed to prompt ambiguity; authors suggest users run their own fairness evaluation.
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; no PDF-stated arXiv id or venue.
OVIS is not strictly zero-shot (its videos are in MOSE).

terms.definition: spatio-temporal mask predicted for an object across video frames
